question: In front of which Keeper's Shrine (土地庙) did the player forge the weapon "Beast Staff · Golden Eye"?

what_worked: The clue fact (shrine location name immediately preceding the forge event) is stored verbatim in a 30-second episode caption, so a single run_sql over the episodes table windowed around the clue interval reliably surfaces it.

All 5 rollouts independently converged on the same episodes row via semantic_search and/or run_sql, indicating the retrieval path is short and robust (low variance question despite 'Medium' temporal_certificate).

Two rollouts (1 and 3) added a clip_qa visual check of the on-screen location label as extra corroboration; this did not change the answer but demonstrates the visual sub-agent correctly reads on-screen Chinese UI text when dispatched to the right timestamp.

Minor transliteration variance across rollouts (e.g. rollout 3 saying 'Firefield/Cool Slope' for 火焰地/清凉坡) did not affect judge scoring since the core entity 'Qingliang Slope' was still present and correctly identified as the shrine.
transferable_lessons: For entity-recognition questions about a specific named location tied to a scripted game event (e.g. an NPC/shrine name shown in an on-screen menu), a direct run_sql over the episodes table windowed on the clue interval is usually sufficient; the 30-second episode captions in this DB tend to name on-screen location labels explicitly.
clip_qa is useful as a cheap corroboration step for on-screen text/UI labels but is not strictly necessary when the episode caption already states the location by name.

Extra semantic_search/run_sql passes beyond the first successful hit (as in rollout 4) add cost without changing the outcome for questions where the clue is this unambiguous; but they did not hurt the score either.
